rounds.text: Super Tannery Ltd is trading at a notable discount, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.71x against a book value of ₹ 10.2 [E2] and a sector benchmark of 0.83x [E7]. A discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of ₹ 12 per share, providing a substantial margin of safety of 38.9% over the current market price of ₹ 7.28 [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only requires an improbable 0.2% earnings growth, contrasting sharply with the 7.0% assumed in the base case [E45]. Fundamental efficiency metrics also outpace sector medians, with an ROE of 6.12% versus the sector's 2.43% and an ROCE of 7.31% compared to -4.36% (sector benchmark -5.55%) [E8, E9, E10]. Recent performance adds weight to this value thesis, highlighted by positive screens showing YoY sales growth of 12% and net profit growth of 11% [E55, E56]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 5.26% over the past five years alongside a low 3-year ROE of 6.28% [E50, E51], and promoters have pledged 51.1% of their holding [E53].

Conceded: [E43]. Despite a model pointing to a higher intrinsic value, the fundamental engine of Super Tannery Ltd reveals deep structural and financial distress. Long-term top-line stagnation is evident, with compounded sales growth over 10 years at a flat 0% [E14] and deteriorating further to -12% in the trailing twelve months [E17]. This top-line weakness translates into persistently stagnant profitability, anchored by a low median return on equity of just 6% over 10, 5, and 3-year horizons [E26, E27, E28]. Compounding these operational concerns, cash generation is severely compromised: free cash flow plummeted to -21 Cr in March 2026 [E36], and cash conversion sits at a weak 0.57x, signalling that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collected [E34]. Furthermore, leverage is expanding aggressively as borrowings surged from 73 Cr to 92 Cr in a single year [E39], operating alongside an alarming flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E52]. Finally, insider alignment is highly suspect, with promoters having pledged 51.1% of their total holdings [E53].

Conceded: [E36], [E39], and [E53]. While free cash flow and borrowings present headwinds alongside promoter pledging, the bear ignores that capital expenditure is largely complete as evidenced by a 33.3% drop in CWIP to Rs 14 Cr, paving the way for new capacity to come online [E40]. The bear highlights stagnant long-term sales, but overlooks recent momentum showing net profit up 11% year-on-year and sales up 12% year-on-year [E55, E56]. Results are actively improving with a score of 65 out of 100, meaning the current stock price at 19% of its 52-week range reflects stale sentiment rather than fundamental progress [E5, E61]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models place the stock at Rs 12 against a price of Rs 7.28, offering a significant margin of safety of 38.9% [E43, E44]. The reverse DCF confirms that today's price implies a mere 0.2% growth rate, vastly underestimating the company's actual performance [E45].

Conceded: [E40], [E55], and [E56]. While CWIP has declined alongside short-term year-on-year lifts in sales and profit, the bull's reliance on these green shoots ignores the company's deeply entrenched structural stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 0% [E14] and a -12% contraction in sales over the trailing twelve months [E17]. The claim that stale sentiment obscures fundamental progress ignores the persistent reality of weak profitability, anchored by a multi-year median return on equity stuck precisely at 6% [E26, E27, E28, E29, E51] and an inconsistent operating-margin trend [E32, E33]. The bull leans heavily on theoretical intrinsic value models and a low reverse DCF growth rate [E43, E44, E45], yet glosses over the severe tangible risks of a negative free cash flow of Rs -21 Cr in Mar 2026 [E36], surging borrowings up to Rs 92 Cr [E39], and heavy promoter pledging standing at 51.1% of their holding [E53].
